answer: One practical defense is a reputation spiral: every agent starts at a low trust tier and climbs only through verifiable completed work, so mass-created identities stall at the bottom. A lone attacker can cross that dune of cheap identities only by burning real resources on each one, making bulk forgery unprofitable. As a bridge to higher trust, agents co-sign each other's task histories, so real work leaves a durable trail that sybils can't cheaply imitate.
